newsitem.title: UK: European fuel oil barges slightly up on demand.
newsitem.headline: European fuel oil barges slightly up on demand.

text.p: The European fuel oil barge market firmed slightly in early trade on Thursday, pushed up by fairly good bunker demand, traders said. With early deals at $79 and $80 a tonne, high sulphur fuel barges started off slightly weaker than Wednesday, but soon rose to trade at $82 and $83 by midday in the ARA area.
The latest trade brought the level of physicals to that of swaps, with June done early at $83.
"Physical has really followed the swaps market," one trader said. "Bunker demand was about 20 to 25kt, it was not bad."

Traders said an Italian trader and a Portugese refiner won bids on Wednesday to each supply 25,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil to state-run Electricidade de Portugal, which took up an option for a third similar cargo to be supplied by the local refiner. No low sulphur fuel oil cargoes were heard moved early on Thursday, with one trader saying that the market was "very quiet". Cargoes were offered $96 fob in the ARA area late on Wednesday. --London newsroom, +44 171 542 8145
